task_instance: Review a small git diff to a Django-style app.py (added get_active_user_count, plus pre-existing N+1 query, SQL injection, and unguarded division) using the Sentry code-review checklist, producing a written review with findings and a verdict.
evidence: Created sample_repo with git init, made two commits (initial version, then a diff adding get_active_user_count and comments marking known issues). Ran `git diff HEAD~1 HEAD -- app.py` to get the actual diff to review. Applied the skill's checklist (runtime errors, performance/ORM N+1, security/SQL injection, test coverage, design, long-term impact) to write /tmp/.../getsentry__skills__code-review/review.md containing: (1) N+1 query finding at app.py get_user_names with a select_related fix, (2) SQL injection finding at get_user_by_id (matches skill's own bad-pattern example) with parameterized-query fix, (3) ZeroDivisionError risk in divide_scores, (4) missing test coverage for the new get_active_user_count function, (5) a minor design question, and a final verdict (request changes, blocking on the SQL injection issue). Verified each finding corresponds to a real line in the diff. No PR posting, --comment, or --fix step was needed for the core deliverable (producing the review); those would require GitHub API access but were not exercised since the task instance was a local diff, consistent with instructions to keep scope minimal and avoid any connector/MCP or external-service writes.
